meaning.long_meaning: Arijit corresponds to the Sanskrit form अरिजित्. Its core lexical sense is conqueror of sorrows. अरिजित् (arijit) means conquering enemies. The source gloss 'Conqueror of sorrows' is not the lexical sense.

faq.a: Arijit corresponds to the Sanskrit form अरिजित्, whose core lexical sense is conqueror of sorrows.

faq.q: What is the origin of Arijit?
faq.a: Arijit is associated with Sanskrit. अरिजित् (arijit) means conquering enemies. The source gloss 'Conqueror of sorrows' is not the lexical sense.
Yes — the underlying form अरिजित् is Sanskrit.
Arijit is used in Hindu naming practice, but Sanskrit origin alone does not make a name Hindu. The classification here rests on documented naming usage.

faq.a: No occurrence of this exact form in the Vedic corpus was verified. Absence of verification is not a claim of absence.

faq.q: How is Arijit written in Indian scripts?
faq.a: Sanskrit अरिजित्, Hindi अरिजित, Marathi अरिजित, Bengali অরিজিৎ, Tamil அரிஜித், Telugu అరిజిత్.
A romanized syllable approximation is a-ri-jit. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
